study_identification_part.si_4_title: Multiscale heterogeneity of functional connectivity in autism

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Three large datasets were pooled: EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP), Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE-I), and Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange II (ABIDE-II). Data collected across 32 scanning sites.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We pooled scans from three large datasets: the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) (Loth et al., 2017) (https://www.eu-aims.eu/ and https://www.aims-2-trials.eu/), and the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchanges I and II, or ABIDE-I and ABIDE-II (Adriana Di Martino et al., 2017; A. Di Martino et al., 2014)"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Ilioska2024.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / Participants, L63-65

answer.LEAP: normative model training (NT) and clinical testing (autism)

answer.ABIDE-I: normative model training (NT) and clinical testing (autism)

answer.ABIDE-II: normative model training (NT) and clinical testing (autism)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Neurotypical (NT) controls from all three datasets were used to train the normative model using 10-fold cross-validation. Autistic individuals from all datasets were then tested against the normative model to quantify FC deviations.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The normative model was trained on the group of neurotypical individuals to establish a normative range for FC and was then tested on the FC maps of the autistic individual's group to quantify the extent of FC deviations from the normative baseline. We quantified the extent of FC deviations in the control group using 10-fold crossvalidation."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Ilioska2024.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / Normative modeling, L87-90

model-1.model-name: Functional connectivity normative model (gaussian process regression)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using 1028 neurotypical controls (EU-AIMS LEAP: 200, ABIDE-I: 481, ABIDE-II: 347). The model was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation on controls.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The final sample included 796 autistic individuals (141 females; age-range: 5-58) and 1028 neuro-typical (NT) individuals (256 females; age-range: 5-56) recruited across 32 different sites." and Table 1: NT n = 1028 (EU-AIMS LEAP: 200, ABIDE-I: 481, ABIDE-II: 347)
